title: Module 6: Asynchronous JavaScript & Event Loop Mechanics (All Chapters)
description: Comprehensive module-level assessment covering all chapters of Module 6: Asynchronous JavaScript & Event Loop Mechanics.

cards.concept: The Callback Pattern & Event Loop Architecture: Microtasks vs Macrotasks Execution Order
cards.question: When a script resolves a Promise and schedules `setTimeout(fn, 0)`, what is the guaranteed execution order in the event loop?

options.text: `setTimeout` callback runs first because timers have top priority.
Microtasks (Promise reactions, queueMicrotask) drain completely immediately after the current call stack clears, before any timer callback runs.
Both run concurrently in libuv's worker thread pool.
The event loop randomly alternates between microtasks and macrotasks.

cards.explanation: Microtasks execute with highest priority as soon as the current synchronous stack empties. The microtask queue must drain to zero before the event loop advances to macrotask phases.
cards.pitfall: Recursively enqueuing microtasks starves the event loop, preventing all I/O, timers, and network responses from executing.
cards.citation: Node.js Event Loop, Timers, and process.nextTick() Official Guide

cards.concept: The Callback Pattern & Event Loop Architecture: Promise.all vs Promise.allSettled Error Semantics
cards.question: In what scenario MUST an engineer use `Promise.allSettled()` instead of `Promise.all()`?

options.text: When running CPU-intensive cryptography on worker threads.
When executing concurrent independent tasks where partial failures should not abort other operations, and full outcome inspection is required.
When tasks must execute strictly sequentially in series.
When promises return primitive values rather than objects.

cards.explanation: Promise.all short-circuits and rejects immediately on the first failure, abandoning remaining promises. Promise.allSettled waits for all promises to complete and returns an array of status objects.
cards.codeSnippet:
const results = await Promise.allSettled([fetchA(), fetchB(), fetchC()]);
const successful = results.filter(r => r.status === 'fulfilled').map(r => r.value);
cards.pitfall: Using Promise.all for independent batch operations causes a single non-critical error to drop all successful parallel operations.
cards.citation: MDN Web Docs: Promise.allSettled() / TC39 Promise Specifications
